evidence_quotes.their_agenda: "what are your biggest concerns and what are the most important things you want answers to on this call today?" — asked before any probing started
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised two concerns (scheduling and furniture reassembly). Nicole acknowledged reassembly capability but did not ask follow-up questions like 'tell me more about the scheduling concerns' or 'what specifically about scheduling matters most to you?'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: "For a typical fifteen by ten storage unit it usually takes around four and a half to six hours... In your case... I estimate your move to take around three to four hours with two movers and one truck, and including the travel fee. It's good the budget around $854 to $1,062." — anchor range provided with personalization to half-full unit and second-floor destination
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: "And would you like our help with your move?" — direct, no softening or built-in out

top_strength: Nicole commanded logistics discovery thoroughly (property type, floor location, walking distances, storage fullness, special items, additional stops all confirmed) and delivered a personalized, anchored estimate with full pricing transparency and both Two Promises clearly explained.
coaching_note: After customers raise concerns in Section 2, dig two layers deep with follow-ups like 'tell me more about that' rather than acknowledge and move on — Nicole didn't explore James's scheduling and reassembly concerns beyond one acknowledgment each, and also skipped the Section 4 'does that feel fair?' pause and the Section 6 genuine final concerns check.
